title: Temporal response profiles — rough PRD scratchpad
content:
Context / one-line idea:
Temporal Response Profiles = a thin layer that lets product teams declare how model responses should change over the *lifetime* of an interaction (time, turns, recency of signals) rather than only by request attributes (model, temperature). Think: first-turn concise answer, mid-session exploratory, late-session summarizer. Profiles are storable, versioned, and referenceable from the API.

Why we care:
- Real apps get different needs as a conversation ages. Customers hack this with brittle client logic or many ad-hoc prompts.
- Centralizing policies improves consistency, telemetry and makes rollouts safer (A/B by profile).
- Ties into cost controls: low-cost profile for background threads, high-fidelity for paid flows.

High level spec sketch:
- Profile object: id, name, description, predicates (turn-index range, last-user-signal recency, explicit tag), actions (model variant, param deltas: temperature/top_p/response_length, prompt wrappers, post-process hooks like compress/summarize), fallback chain.
- API: attach profile by explicit profile_id OR use auto-routing rules (profile selectors) in project config.
- Runtime: lightweight evaluation before serving; output telemetry tag (profile=xyz, matched_predicate).
- Versioning: profiles are versioned + can be pinned to a rollout rule.

User stories (rough):
- Product manager: "I want first-response brevity for new users and richer responses later if they ask follow-ups."
- Platform engineer: "I want a way to create a low-cost fallback profile for idle sessions to reduce spend."
- Customer support: "Pin a profile that enforces stricter safety filters during certain hours."

Acceptance criteria / success signals:
- API: create/read/update/delete profile + attach to route in <1 week dev time for MVP.
- Runtime: profile evaluation adds <3ms median overhead to request path.
- Telemetry: profiles show up in console, and we can slice latency/cost/quality by profile.
- Experiment: run profile A/B (profile vs no-profile) and measure user engagement + cost delta over 2 weeks.

UX notes (console):
- Profile builder: simple toggles for common presets (concise, verbose, summarizer, safety-strict).
- Advanced: rule builder with drag-and-drop predicates (turn-count, latest-user-signal age, session-tag).
- Preview: run a sample session and step through turns with profile applied.

API implications / edge cases:
- When to apply: explicit profile_id parameter should override auto-route.
- Composability with rollouts: profile should be first-class in rollout rules (canary by profile).
- Conflicts: merging multiple matched profiles -> precedence rules (explicit > pinned > auto; higher priority numeric).
- Server-side prompt templates: template variables for profile-level metadata (e.g., "profile_stage").

Instrumentation / metrics to emit:
- profile.match_count, profile.avg_latency, profile.avg_cost_per_request, profile.quality_regressions (via eval hooks), profile.fallback_rate.

Prototype experiments (small, quick wins):
1) CLI-only: allow a route to attach a 2-stage profile (turn 0 concise, turn>=3 verbose) and test with 5 customers.
2) Auto-profile by inactivity: if last user turn > 10m, apply a low-cost profile.
3) Safety-scheduled: prototype schedule-based predicate (apply strict-safety profile between 23:00-05:00 UTC).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Predicate language: initial set (turn-index, time-since-last-user, session-tag, user-tier). Do we need arbitrary CEL? Complexity vs support cost.
- Storage & scale: profiles are small but lookup must be fast for high QPS. Cache and local replicate on nodes? TTL invalidation on updates.
- Client vs server enforcement: allow client-side hints but server enforces. How to surface mismatch warnings?
- Migration: how to help customers migrate from ad-hoc prompt templates into profiles? CLI import tool?

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Another surface area to test/monitor; risk of users misconfiguring and degrading quality. Mitigation: ship safe defaults & preview.
- Overfitting to turn-index heuristics may be brittle for multi-agent or multiplexed sessions. Need generic predicates.

Rollout thoughts:
- Alpha: internal -> select partners (3) with onboarding help; collect telemetry + qualitative feedback.
- Beta: console builder enabled, profile analytics, 1-month trial.
- GA: SLA and full audit logs, exportable profile history.

Notes to self:
- Talk to Sam about console mini-builder feasibility (ticket PLAT-1122).
- Ask Mika about runtime cache strategy and cost estimate for profile lookups.
- Draft a tiny confluence explainer with examples: support that shows before/after cost and latency.

Quick sketch example (pseudo):
Profile "starter-brief": predicates: turn_index == 0; actions: model: "open-1x-small", max_tokens: 120, temperature: 0.2, prompt_wrapper: "answer_brief"
Profile "deep-dive": predicates: turn_index >= 3 OR session_tag == \"expert\"; actions: model: "open-1x-highfidelity", max_tokens: 800, temperature: 0.8

If this lands well, next step: design profile schema + minimal API and wire up console builder prototype.

-- neha (brain dump)
